description: A coalition of European academic labs and civic tech groups releases a federated training framework that enables distributed fine-tuning of open models on sensitive public data without centralizing it, bypassing both privacy regulations and export controls. The framework gains rapid adoption in municipal services, accelerating local AI deployment but deepening fragmentation in the Union's sovereign stack.

A split emerges among EU member states over the enforcement of the AI Act's high-risk provisions, with three smaller states formally requesting exemptions for public-sector AI use in welfare and law enforcement, citing administrative burden and local legal traditions. The European Commission opens infringement proceedings, but the political cost of enforcement rises as the audit initiative stalls.
